image_description: A vintage blue typewriter viewed from a high angle. The image features the full keyboard deck, carriage return lever, paper bail, and a sheet of white paper inserted in the platen. A light blue document holder is attached to the left side. The focus is on the mechanical structure of the typewriter, specifically the round keys and the elongated space bar at the bottom center.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Elongated rectangular key spanning the full width of the bottom keyboard row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is present but does not span the 'full width' of the row; it is centrally located between shift/lock keys, which is standard for typewriters but contradicts the literal 'full width' description often applied to modern PC keyboards.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Length is dramatically greater than any other key, roughly ten times the width of a standard letter key.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is visibly the longest key, approximately 6-8 times the width of the adjacent round typebars, satisfying the 'dramatically greater' criteria.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Surface is flat or slightly concave.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The visible top surface of the space bar appears flat with rounded edges, consistent with vintage typewriter design.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Underside connects to a long stabilizer bar mechanism.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The underside and internal stabilizer mechanism are completely occluded by the keycap and the keyboard deck structure.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Label is typically blank with no printed character.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is clearly blank, lacking any text or symbols, unlike some modifier keys which may have labels.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Positioned centrally between modifier keys on the bottom row.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is correctly positioned in the center of the bottom row, flanked by what appear to be shift or margin release levers/keys.
The key appears to be made of smooth material (likely plastic or bakelite) with a non-glossy, matte finish consistent with the rest of the keyboard.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Typically white, black, or gray to match keyboard color scheme.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The space bar is an off-white/cream color, matching the other keytops and contrasting with the dark blue body of the typewriter.

checkpoint_verdicts.checkpoint: Part of a standard computer or typewriter keyboard.
checkpoint_verdicts.reasoning: The object is clearly integrated into a functional typewriter keyboard assembly.

artifact_observations.location: Gold emblem on the right side of the typewriter body
artifact_observations.reasoning: The gold script/logo on the right panel is illegible and morphologically inconsistent, resembling AI-generated gibberish rather than a coherent brand name.
